chapter_summary: Proverbs 22 opens with two of the most important statements in wisdom literature: that a good name is worth more than riches, and that God made both the rich and the poor. It then moves through a rich sweep of themes — the rewards of humility and the fear of the Lord, the wise person who sees danger and avoids it, the foundational command to train children in the right way, the danger of debt, the generosity that brings blessing, and the importance of learning from wise teachers. The chapter closes with a series of practical warnings and commands: do not cheat the poor, avoid angry companions, do not take on others' debts carelessly, do not move ancient boundaries, and pursue excellence in your work. At its heart, Proverbs 22 is a chapter about formation — shaping character, reputation, and wisdom from childhood so that they last a lifetime.
main_lesson: A good name and a humble heart are worth more than gold. God cares for everyone, and He blesses those who are generous, wise, and honest.

memory_verse.kjv: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
memory_verse.little_bible: Teach a child the right way to live. When they grow old, they will not forget it.

parent_guide:
Proverbs 22 opens the final section of the main Solomonic collection (chapters 10–22:16) before a shorter section of sayings from 'the wise' begins in 22:17. The chapter's opening verse on a good name versus great riches is one of the most famous lines in all of Proverbs — it asks children to consider what truly matters about a person. Verse 6 ('Train up a child') is arguably the most well-known parenting verse in Scripture, and its appearance here is significant: it places the responsibility of formation squarely on the parent. The method of training in view is not mere instruction but shaping the whole direction of a child's life — the word 'way' carries the sense of a bent, inclination, or habit. A child trained toward wisdom, honesty, and the fear of the Lord will have a foundation that outlasts every other influence.

The most important things to communicate to your child from this chapter are: (1) What makes you valuable to God and others is not how much money you have, but what kind of person you are. (2) God made every person — rich or poor — and every person deserves to be treated with dignity. (3) Generous people are blessed. Selfish people eventually lose everything. (4) Wise people see trouble coming and avoid it; they do not just wander into danger. (5) Choose your friends carefully — angry, foolish people will shape you if you spend too much time with them.

For application, the verse on training children (v.6) is worth lingering on together. What is the 'way' your family is training your children toward? Is your home a place where Scripture, prayer, generosity, and honesty are the daily curriculum — not just occasional events? The habits formed in childhood are the strongest habits of all.

For cross-reference and deeper study: Proverbs 22:6 connects to Deuteronomy 6:4–9 (the Shema — the command to teach children God's words diligently). Verses 22–23 echo the special concern for the poor found throughout Proverbs and the prophets (see Amos 5:12; James 2:6). The section on wise sayings beginning at verse 17 draws on a broader ancient Near Eastern wisdom tradition, pointing to the universal nature of wisdom across cultures while maintaining its rootedness in the fear of the Lord.
application_for_children: This week, think about your name. What do people say about you when you are not there? Ask God to help you build a name that means: kind, honest, and wise. And look for one person you can be generous to today.

verses.kjv: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.
verses.little_bible: A good name is worth more than great riches. Being loved and trusted is better than silver or gold.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A good name is worth more than riches.
verses.meaning: Reputation — the kind of person others know you to be — is of greater value than accumulated wealth. 'Loving favour' means the goodwill and affection of others, which cannot be purchased. A good name is built through character, honesty, and faithfulness over time. This proverb challenges the common assumption that wealth is the highest goal.
verses.prayer: God, help me build a good name by living right.
verses.discussion_question: What makes someone's name worth remembering?
verses.family_discussion: What do we want our family name to mean to others? What habits and choices are building — or damaging — the name we carry right now?
verses.do_it_today: Ask a parent: 'What is one thing about our family name you want to protect?' Listen carefully to the answer.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child holding their name in glowing letters above two piles of gold coins, the name shining brighter than all the gold, warm watercolour style

verses.kjv: The rich and poor meet together: the LORD is the maker of them all.
verses.little_bible: Rich people and poor people both come from God. He made them all. Every person is equal before God.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God made both rich and poor equally.
verses.meaning: Wealth does not make one person more valuable to God than another. The phrase 'meet together' suggests that in God's sight, all people stand on level ground. God is the creator of all people regardless of their economic condition — a profound equality before the Creator.
verses.prayer: God, help me treat every person as someone You made.
verses.discussion_question: How should we treat people who have less than us?
verses.family_discussion: How do we actively counter the tendency to value people by their wealth or status — in the friendships we make, the conversations we have, and the stories we tell our children?
verses.do_it_today: Look at every person you meet today and remember: God made that person. Treat them that way.
verses.illustration_prompt: A rich child and a poor child standing side by side, both equally loved, a warm divine light shining on them both, gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: A prudent man foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself: but the simple pass on, and are punished.
verses.little_bible: A wise person sees danger coming and stays away from it. But a foolish person walks right into it and gets hurt.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wise people see danger and avoid it.
verses.meaning: Prudence — the ability to look ahead and anticipate consequences — is a mark of wisdom. The wise person does not wait to see if danger is real; they act on what they see coming. The 'simple' person lacks this foresight and pays the price. Wisdom involves seeing not just the present moment but the likely future.
verses.prayer: God, give me wisdom to see trouble and stay safe.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to see danger coming?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate foresight in our children — the habit of thinking ahead about where a choice leads before they make it?
verses.do_it_today: Before you do something today, ask: 'Where might this lead?' Choose the path you can see ends well.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child pausing at a fork in the road, seeing storm clouds ahead on one path and turning away wisely, sunny watercolour scene

verses.kjv: By humility and the fear of the LORD are riches, and honour, and life.
verses.little_bible: When you are humble and you respect God, He gives you what truly matters. He gives riches, honour, and real life.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Humility and fear of God bring true blessing.
verses.meaning: The combination of humility (lowliness of self) and the fear of the Lord (awe and reverence for God) is the path to genuine blessing — riches (which may be material or spiritual), honour (recognition of worth), and life (the full life God intends). These are not earned but flow naturally from a heart rightly oriented toward God.
verses.prayer: God, make me humble so I can receive Your best.
verses.discussion_question: What does being humble mean to you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model and teach humility in a culture that rewards self-promotion? What does a humble family look and sound like?
verses.do_it_today: Do something kind today without telling anyone about it. That is one way to practise humility.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child kneeling humbly in prayer, golden light of blessing and honour resting gently on their head, watercolour scene of quiet reverence

verses.kjv: Thorns and snares are in the way of the froward: he that doth keep his soul shall be far from them.
verses.little_bible: The path of someone who does wrong is full of traps. But the person who guards their heart stays far from all that danger.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Guard your heart to stay safe from traps.
verses.meaning: The 'froward' — twisted, perverse — person walks a path full of thorns and snares: obstacles and traps. The person who 'keeps his soul' (guards their inner life, their heart, their choices) will be kept far from these dangers. The path you choose determines what dangers you encounter.
verses.prayer: God, help me guard my heart from wrong paths.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to guard your heart?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to recognise and resist the 'traps' that lead them away from the right path — in media, friendships, and habits?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one thing today that could be a trap for you. Choose to walk away from it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A path with thorns and hidden snares on one side, and a child walking safely on a clear smooth path on the other, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
verses.little_bible: Teach a child the right way to live. When they grow old, they will not forget it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Teach children God's way early — it lasts forever.
verses.meaning: One of the most significant verses in all of Proverbs for parents. The command to 'train up' carries the sense of shaping, directing, dedicating — not merely instructing. 'The way he should go' refers to the path of wisdom, righteousness, and the fear of the Lord. The promise is remarkable: early formation in the right direction creates a deep disposition that outlasts every later influence. This does not mean children will never stray, but that the right training creates a powerful return point.
verses.prayer: God, help my parents teach me the right way.
verses.discussion_question: Who teaches you the right way to live?
verses.family_discussion: What is the 'way' we are actively training our children in — not just by telling them but by the daily habits, rhythms, and values of our home?
verses.do_it_today: Parents: take five minutes today to teach your child one specific wisdom principle. Children: ask a parent to teach you something wise.
verses.illustration_prompt: A parent and young child walking together on a bright path, the parent gently guiding the child's steps, warm golden light ahead, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The rich ruleth over the poor, and the borrower is servant to the lender.
verses.little_bible: Wealthy people have power over those with less. And when you borrow money, you become like a servant to the one you borrowed from.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Borrowing makes you a servant to the lender.
verses.meaning: This proverb is an honest observation about power and debt. Wealth confers power in this world. And debt creates a form of bondage — the borrower's choices become constrained by obligation to the lender. This is not a command but a warning: debt has real consequences on your freedom. Wisdom teaches us to live within our means.
verses.prayer: God, help me be wise about money and not a slave to debt.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when you owe someone something?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children a healthy, biblical attitude toward money, debt, and financial wisdom — avoiding both fear and carelessness?
verses.do_it_today: If you have borrowed something from someone, return it today or make a plan to do so.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with chains of obligation connecting them to someone they owe, looking downward, contrasted with a free child walking lightly with nothing owed, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: He that soweth iniquity shall reap vanity: and the rod of his anger shall fail.
verses.little_bible: If you plant seeds of wrong, you will grow nothing worth having. And using anger to hurt others will always fail in the end.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wrong choices grow into worthless results.
verses.meaning: The harvest principle applied to sin: you reap what you sow. Those who sow wickedness and injustice reap emptiness and futility — nothing of lasting value. The 'rod of his anger' — the power they wield through rage and cruelty — will eventually break and fail. Sin is ultimately unproductive.
verses.prayer: God, help me plant good seeds with all my choices.
verses.discussion_question: What do you think happens when you plant bad seeds?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children make the connection between present choices and future outcomes — to think like farmers, not just consumers?
verses.do_it_today: Name one good seed you can plant today — a kind word, an honest action, a helpful deed. Do it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child planting dark seeds that grow into empty withered stalks, versus another child planting bright seeds that grow into abundant fruit, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.
verses.little_bible: The person with a generous heart will be blessed. They give their own food to someone who has none.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Generous people are blessed by God.
verses.meaning: A 'bountiful eye' is a generous, open-hearted way of looking at the world — seeing others' needs and responding. The specific act here is sharing bread — food — with the poor. Generosity is both a character trait and a blessing-receiving posture: those who give generously receive God's blessing in return.
verses.prayer: God, give me a generous heart for those with less.
verses.discussion_question: How can you share what you have with someone who needs it?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate a culture of generosity in our home — giving as a normal and joyful habit, not a reluctant or special occasion?
verses.do_it_today: Find something you can give away today — food, time, or a kind word — to someone who needs it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sharing their bread with a smaller child who has nothing, both smiling, a warm divine blessing visible over them, gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Cast out the scorner, and contention shall go out; yea, strife and reproach shall cease.
verses.little_bible: Remove the mocker from the group and the fighting will stop. Arguments and shame leave with the mocker.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Remove the mocker and peace returns.
verses.meaning: The scorner or mocker is a source of division and conflict. Remarkably, removing one person — the one who mocks others and dismisses wisdom — resolves strife, contention, and shame all at once. This is a principle about the outsized negative influence of a single person who treats things sacred as ridiculous.
verses.prayer: God, keep me from being a mocker. Help me bring peace.
verses.discussion_question: Why does a mocker make everything harder for everyone?
verses.family_discussion: How do we identify and address the 'scorner' dynamic in our children's peer groups — and in our own family conversations?
verses.do_it_today: Choose not to mock or make fun of anything serious today. See if the atmosphere around you becomes more peaceful.
verses.illustration_prompt: A group of children in tension with one mocking figure in the middle, then peace returning as the group finds calm without the source of mockery, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: He that loveth pureness of heart, for the grace of his lips the king shall be his friend.
verses.little_bible: The person with a pure heart and kind words will have even great leaders as their friend.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A pure heart and kind words win great friends.
verses.meaning: Purity of heart (an inner life free from malice, deceit, and selfish ambition) combined with gracious speech (words that are fitting, kind, and wise) wins the admiration and friendship of even the greatest people. Character opens doors that wealth and power alone cannot. This speaks to the universally compelling quality of genuine goodness.
verses.prayer: God, give me a pure heart and kind words.
verses.discussion_question: Why do kind words help people trust you?
verses.family_discussion: How are we developing both inner purity and gracious speech in our children — the combination that opens doors and wins the right kind of friendships?
verses.do_it_today: Speak one gracious, kind word to someone today — a word that comes from a genuinely good heart.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child speaking with kindness to a leader figure, the leader leaning in with a warm smile of friendship, light radiating from the child's honest heart, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The eyes of the LORD preserve knowledge, and he overthroweth the words of the transgressor.
verses.little_bible: God watches over and protects truth. He tears down the lies of those who disobey Him.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God protects truth and destroys lies.
verses.meaning: God is actively engaged in preserving knowledge — the body of truth and wisdom He has revealed. He is equally active in overthrowing the words of those who sin and distort truth. This is a profound assurance: truth does not need our defence as much as it needs our faithfulness — God himself guards it.
verses.prayer: God, thank You for protecting what is true.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean that God watches over truth?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop a deep confidence that God's truth does not need to be defended anxiously — because He is its guardian?
verses.do_it_today: When you hear something false today, quietly trust that God knows the truth and stands by it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A pair of divine eyes watching over glowing scrolls of truth, while dark words crumble to dust below them, peaceful watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: The slothful man saith, There is a lion without, I shall be slain in the streets.
verses.little_bible: The lazy person says, 'There is a lion outside! I cannot go out!' He makes up excuses to avoid doing the work.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Lazy people always find excuses not to work.
verses.meaning: The lazy person's excuse is absurdly extreme — a lion in the streets — revealing that sloth invents reasons to avoid work rather than engaging with real obstacles. The proverb gently mocks this by choosing the most dramatic possible excuse. Laziness is not just inactivity — it is creative avoidance.
verses.memory_phrase: No excuses. Just do the work.
verses.prayer: God, help me not make excuses when there is work to do.
verses.discussion_question: What is a made-up excuse you have heard — or used — to avoid something hard?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children recognise the difference between a real obstacle and a made-up excuse — and develop the courage to push through both?
verses.do_it_today: If there is something you have been avoiding, stop making excuses today and take one step toward doing it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A lazy child pointing dramatically at an imaginary lion outside the window while chores sit undone inside, humorous watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The mouth of strange women is a deep pit: he that is abhorred of the LORD shall fall therein.
verses.little_bible: Being tricked by the wrong kind of words is like falling into a deep hole. Those who turn away from God fall into such traps.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Wrong words are a deep trap for the unwary.
verses.meaning: This proverb warns against seductive, flattering, or deceiving speech from those who would lead one away from God's path. The 'deep pit' imagery conveys that such entrapment is serious and difficult to escape. Those who have turned away from God are especially vulnerable — they have already weakened their defences against spiritual danger. Parents should note: the warning applies to any speech or influence that draws a person away from God's way.
verses.prayer: God, help me stay away from voices that lead me wrong.
verses.discussion_question: How can you tell if a voice or friend is leading you toward God or away from Him?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to evaluate the voices and influences in their lives — to recognise when something sounds appealing but leads to a deep pit?
verses.do_it_today: Think of the voices you listen to most. Do they lead you toward God? Make sure the most important voices are the right ones.
verses.illustration_prompt: A deep dark pit surrounded by deceptive beautiful words, a figure on the edge being lured by flattery, warned away by a guiding light, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.
verses.little_bible: Every child is born with foolishness inside. But loving correction drives the foolishness away and helps the child grow wise.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Children need loving correction to grow wise.
verses.meaning: This verse is honest about the nature of children: foolishness is not an occasional visitor but is 'bound' — tied — in the child's heart. This is not a counsel of despair but a call to consistent, loving correction. The 'rod of correction' is the instrument of disciplined guidance that removes foolishness and creates space for wisdom to grow. Correction is not cruelty — it is love taking the long view.
verses.prayer: God, thank You for parents who correct me with love.
verses.discussion_question: Why is being corrected sometimes a gift, not a punishment?
verses.family_discussion: How do we practise consistent, loving correction in our home — firm enough to drive out foolishness, warm enough to keep our children's hearts open to us?
verses.do_it_today: When someone corrects you today, say 'thank you' and mean it. They are trying to help you grow wise.
verses.illustration_prompt: A parent gently but firmly correcting a child, foolishness shown as a dark shadow leaving the child, wisdom beginning to glow in its place, loving warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: He that oppresseth the poor to increase his riches, and he that giveth to the rich, shall surely come to want.
verses.little_bible: Cheating poor people to make yourself richer will backfire. Giving gifts to the rich to get what you want will also end in loss.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Cheating the poor and bribing the rich both lead to loss.
verses.meaning: Two forms of injustice are condemned: oppressing the poor for personal gain, and giving bribes to the rich to curry favour. Both are forms of using wealth wrongly — one by taking from those who have nothing, the other by paying to gain advantage from those who have everything. Both will result in the perpetrator coming to poverty themselves. God's justice inverts these schemes.
verses.prayer: God, help me never gain from hurting someone with less.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it especially wrong to cheat someone who is already poor?
verses.family_discussion: How do we instil in our children a specific commitment to fairness toward those who cannot defend themselves — the poor, the young, the overlooked?
verses.do_it_today: Make sure that nothing you gain today comes at someone else's unfair expense. If it does, make it right.
verses.illustration_prompt: A person with a large money bag pressing down on a small poor figure, while their own bag begins to empty and shrink, God's justice quietly visible, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Bow down thine ear, and hear the words of the wise, and apply thine heart unto my knowledge.
verses.little_bible: Lean in and listen to the words of the wise. Let what they say reach your heart and change you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Lean in and truly listen to wisdom.
verses.meaning: The image of 'bowing the ear' is one of attentive, humble listening — physically leaning toward the speaker. Wisdom is not just heard casually; it must be received into the heart and applied. This marks the beginning of a new section in Proverbs (the 'thirty sayings of the wise') that calls for a deliberate posture of receptive learning.
verses.prayer: God, help me truly listen and let wisdom reach my heart.
verses.discussion_question: What does it look like to really listen — not just hear?
verses.family_discussion: Are we creating moments in our family where real listening happens — not background noise but genuine heart-to-heart teaching and receiving?
verses.do_it_today: When someone speaks wisdom to you today, physically lean in. Let your body show that you are truly listening.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child leaning their ear toward a wise elder, eyes wide and attentive, the words flowing into their heart like warm light, gentle watercolour scene

verses.kjv: For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee; they shall withal be fitted in thy lips.
verses.little_bible: It is a wonderful thing to hold wisdom inside you. When you do, wise words come out of your mouth ready and waiting.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Keep wisdom inside and it comes out when needed.
verses.meaning: Internalising wisdom produces a beautiful result: it becomes natural in speech. When wisdom lives within you, you do not have to struggle to find the right words — they are already there. This is the outcome of the diligent listening called for in verse 17.
verses.prayer: God, let Your wisdom live inside me every day.
verses.discussion_question: How can you store wisdom inside yourself so it is ready when you need it?
verses.family_discussion: What are we filling our children's inner lives with — the things that will come out of their mouths in pressure moments? Scripture memorisation is one powerful answer.
verses.do_it_today: Memorise one verse today. It is now inside you, ready when you need it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with a warm glowing store of wisdom inside their chest, words ready and bright on their lips, peaceful and prepared expression, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: That thy trust may be in the LORD, I have made known to thee this day, even to thee.
verses.little_bible: All these words are written so that you will trust in God. Yes — these words are for you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God's wisdom is given so you will trust Him.
verses.meaning: The stated purpose of this section of wisdom is explicit: not merely education, not just practical living tips, but that the reader would place their trust in the Lord. Wisdom's goal is always personal relationship with God — faith and trust, not just knowledge. The phrase 'even to thee' is remarkably personal — it is addressed to you, specifically.
verses.prayer: God, all this wisdom is so I will trust You more.
verses.discussion_question: Why does God give us wisdom — what does He want us to do with it?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children see that all the wisdom we teach them points toward one goal: trusting God, not just being well-behaved?
verses.do_it_today: Say out loud: 'God, I trust You today.' Then act on that trust in one specific way.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child holding an open book, wisdom words rising from the pages toward God, a connection of trust forming between the child and heaven, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Have not I written to thee excellent things in counsels and knowledge,
verses.little_bible: God has written excellent things for you. He gives you the very best advice and knowledge.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God gives us His very best wisdom.
verses.meaning: The writer affirms that what has been given is not ordinary advice but 'excellent things' — a collection of thirty carefully crafted wisdom sayings. God, through inspired wisdom, has provided more than enough counsel for a well-lived life. The rhetorical question expects the answer: yes, He has.
verses.memory_phrase: God gives His best to us.
verses.prayer: God, thank You for sharing Your best wisdom with me.
verses.discussion_question: What is the most excellent piece of advice you have ever heard?
verses.family_discussion: How do we communicate to our children that Scripture is not a rule book but a treasure — God's very best given to them personally?
verses.do_it_today: Read one verse of the Bible today and ask: 'What is excellent about this? What does God want me to do with this?'
verses.illustration_prompt: An open glowing scroll with words shining like gold, held out as a gift from above, a child receiving it with wide and grateful eyes, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: That I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth; that thou mightest answer the words of truth to them that send unto thee?
verses.little_bible: So that you will know for certain that God's words are true. And so you can share that truth with others when they ask.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Know the truth so you can share it with others.
verses.meaning: Two purposes are named: first, personal certainty — the individual reader knowing with confidence that God's Word is true and reliable. Second, outward communication — being equipped to give true answers to those who come asking. Wisdom is not just for private benefit but for the benefit of others who need truth.
verses.prayer: God, let me know Your truth so I can share it.
verses.discussion_question: Who could you share one true thing from God's Word with today?
verses.family_discussion: How do we equip our children not just to know wisdom for themselves but to be able to give truthful, clear answers to others — friends, classmates, neighbours?
verses.do_it_today: Find one true thing from Scripture today. Then find someone to share it with before the day ends.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with a glowing truth in their hands, turning to share it with another child who is waiting and wondering, warm light passing between them, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Rob not the poor, because he is poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:
verses.little_bible: Do not steal from the poor just because they cannot fight back. Do not hurt those who are already hurting.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Never take from those who cannot defend themselves.
verses.meaning: The gate was the place of legal proceedings in ancient cities — where verdicts were given and disputes settled. The command not to oppress the afflicted 'in the gate' is a direct prohibition against using legal or social power to crush those who are already vulnerable. Taking advantage of weakness is a particular form of injustice that God explicitly forbids.
verses.prayer: God, help me protect those who are weak, not hurt them.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it especially wrong to hurt someone who is already struggling?
verses.family_discussion: Where are the 'gates' in our children's world — the places of authority or power where the weak can be taken advantage of? How do we teach them to stand against that?
verses.do_it_today: Stand up for someone weaker than you today. Do not let them be taken advantage of if you can help it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child standing protectively beside a smaller, poorer child, shielding them from an imposing figure trying to take advantage, courageous watercolour scene

verses.kjv: For the LORD will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those that spoiled them.
verses.little_bible: God will stand up and fight for the poor. He will deal with those who hurt them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God fights for the poor and oppressed.
verses.meaning: The reason not to oppress the poor is not just moral principle — it is because God is their advocate and defender. He will 'plead their cause' in the highest court. And He will do to their oppressors what they did to the poor — spoil the soul of those who spoiled them. This is God's justice: precise and inevitable.
verses.prayer: God, thank You for defending those who have no one else.
verses.discussion_question: Why can poor people trust that they are not alone?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop a vision of God as the great advocate and defender of the poor — not distant and uncaring but personally engaged in justice?
verses.do_it_today: Pray specifically for one person or group being treated unjustly today. Trust that God hears and will act.
verses.illustration_prompt: God's hand reaching down in defence of a small poor figure, a bright shield of divine protection around them, justice radiating from above, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Make no friendship with an angry man; and with a furious man thou shalt not go:
verses.little_bible: Do not become friends with someone who is always angry. Do not spend time with someone who loses control with rage.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not make friends with an angry, furious person.
verses.meaning: The choice of companions is critically important. An angry, furious person is described here as someone to actively avoid — not just once, but in ongoing relationship. The reason follows in the next verse: their ways will rub off on you. This is an honest warning about the shaping power of those we spend time with.
verses.prayer: God, help me choose friends who are calm and wise.
verses.discussion_question: How do the people you spend time with affect the way you act?
verses.family_discussion: How do we guide our children toward friendships that build them up — and wisely away from friendships that will pull them in destructive directions?
verses.do_it_today: Look at your closest friendships. Do they make you calmer and wiser — or more angry and reckless? Pray about what you find.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child turning away from a furious, scowling figure, choosing instead to walk toward a calm, smiling friend, clear path ahead, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Lest thou learn his ways, and get a snare to thy soul.
verses.little_bible: If you do, you will start to act like them. And that will trap your own soul.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Angry friends teach you their angry ways.
verses.meaning: This verse gives the reason for the warning in verse 24: imitation is powerful. Prolonged exposure to an angry person's patterns will result in adopting those patterns — and that adopted anger becomes a trap that entangles the soul. Bad habits learned from companions can become permanent characteristics.
verses.prayer: God, protect me from picking up bad habits from others.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever started acting like someone you spent a lot of time with?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand — in practical terms — that they are always being shaped by who they spend time with, whether they notice it or not?
verses.do_it_today: Think about one habit or attitude you have picked up from someone around you. Is it a good one? Keep it. Is it bad? Choose to drop it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child slowly taking on the posture and expression of an angry companion beside them, a visible snare forming around their feet, cautionary watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: Be not thou one of them that strike hands, or of them that are sureties for debts:
verses.little_bible: Do not make a promise to pay someone else's debt. Do not put your hand to a deal that is not yours to carry.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not promise to pay someone else's debts.
verses.meaning: 'Striking hands' was the ancient gesture sealing a financial guarantee — a surety or pledge. The warning here is against carelessly taking on financial responsibility for another person's debts. This does not prohibit all generosity, but warns against making binding financial commitments you cannot control or fulfil.
verses.prayer: God, help me be careful and wise with every promise I make.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to only promise what you can keep?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children the weight of a promise — that their word is their bond, and they should not commit to more than they can deliver?
verses.do_it_today: Only make promises today that you fully intend and are able to keep. If you cannot keep an old one, address it honestly.
verses.illustration_prompt: Two figures shaking hands over a debt contract, one looking worried and trapped, a caution symbol visible, wise figure stepping back from the handshake, watercolour illustration

verses.kjv: If thou hast nothing to pay, why should he take away thy bed from under thee?
verses.little_bible: If you have nothing to pay back, you could lose even your bed. Debt can take the last thing you have.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Careless debt can cost you everything.
verses.meaning: The rhetorical question makes the consequence of unwise surety vivid and personal: if the debt cannot be paid, the creditor will come for everything — even the bed under you. This is a practical warning about the real-world consequence of financial carelessness. Wisdom protects the most basic security of home and rest.
verses.prayer: God, help me live wisely so I always have enough.
verses.discussion_question: What happens when you borrow more than you can ever give back?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to live within their means — to value the security of owing nothing over the temporary pleasure of having more?
verses.do_it_today: Think about whether you owe anyone anything — money, time, a favour. Make a plan to make it right.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child looking at an empty room with just a bare floor, their bed having been taken away because of unpaid debt, a lesson in consequences, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Remove not the ancient landmark, which thy fathers have set.
verses.little_bible: Do not move the old boundary markers your parents and grandparents put in place. They are there for a reason.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Honour the boundaries your parents set.
verses.meaning: Landmark stones marked property boundaries in ancient Israel. Moving them was effectively stealing — taking land by stealth rather than force. The command preserves not only property rights but also the legacy of previous generations. In a broader sense, this proverb warns against tearing down the established, inherited wisdom and boundaries set by those who came before, simply for personal gain.
verses.prayer: God, help me honour the wisdom of those before me.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important not to change rules that protect people?
verses.family_discussion: What are the 'landmarks' — boundaries, values, and inheritances — that our family has been given and needs to protect for the next generation?
verses.do_it_today: Ask a grandparent or older relative about one important value they want to pass down to you. Write it down and keep it.
verses.illustration_prompt: An ancient stone boundary marker standing firm in a green field, a child placing their hand on it with respect, honouring what was set before them, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.
verses.little_bible: If you see someone who works hard and with great skill, watch out! That person will stand before kings one day. They will not stay unnoticed.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Excellent, diligent work leads to great honour.
verses.meaning: Excellence and diligence in one's work is ultimately recognised and rewarded at the highest level — 'before kings.' The person who applies themselves with skill and thoroughness to their calling will rise far above those who remain obscure and mediocre. This is not a promise of fame but of the universal principle that excellent work rises to the top. It is one of the most encouraging closing notes in the wisdom literature: do your work excellently and it will not go unseen.
verses.prayer: God, help me do my best work in everything I do.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to do your very best at something?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate a spirit of excellence — not perfectionism or anxiety — but wholehearted, skilled effort in everything our children do, for the glory of God?
verses.do_it_today: Pick one thing you will do today and do it with excellence. Not just okay — but your very best.
verses.illustration_prompt: A diligent child working with skill and care at a craft, the work glowing with quality, a king or great leader looking on with admiration in the distance, watercolour illustration
